title: JuliusBrussee/caveman
lede: Caveman is a skill plus local proxy for coding agents that makes the model reply in clipped, article-free English and compresses what it reads, to cut token spend without touching code or your prompts.

points: The voice rules shorten answers while keeping code, commands, paths and error messages verbatim; user prompts are never rewritten.
A read-side layer shrinks logs, JSON, CSV, YAML and test output before the model sees them; the README reports 33.2% fewer input tokens per session, with HTML not yet handled.
Auto picks the model and effort per request; an interim 85-task run scored close to Opus 5.5 at xhigh effort for under half the cost.
Blocks saves the scripts an agent writes so it reuses them instead of retyping them every session.
Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and, per the README, 30+ other agents.

points.text: Modes not taking effect on some hosts, such as ultracave on Opus 5.5 and in Visual Studio Copilot.
TypeScript and Python middleware adapters fail their canaries against new framework releases.
Print mode (claude -p) misses the compression that interactive sessions get.
Packaging requests, starting with Nix support.
